scenes.headline: How FlashState lets a hybrid model resume an agent turn
scenes.sub: Exact-end checkpoints, priced by the prefill they save.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Breadcrumb! A hybrid model resumes a cached prompt only from a snapshot taken at that exact token. Here's how FlashState picks them.

scenes.text: Save the recurrent checkpoint exactly where each agent turn ends, and keep or evict it together with the KV it depends on.
scenes.mark: exactly where each agent turn ends
scenes.say: The idea: checkpoint exactly where each turn ends, and keep or evict it together with the cache it needs.

scenes.title: What a hybrid model needs to resume

steps.say: Attention layers keep keys and values per token, so any prefix is already cached.
Linear layers overwrite one state as they read. It can't be rolled back.
So FlashState snapshots it exactly where the turn ends, even mid-block.
Snapshot plus cache is one hybrid state. The next turn resumes there.

left.title: Stock vLLM
left.say: Stock vLLM checkpoints only at block boundaries, so each turn recomputes a gap.

right.title: FlashState
items: Checkpoint at the exact turn end
State and its KV leave together
right.say: FlashState resumes at the exact end, and evicts state and cache together.

scenes.title: One price for keeping a state
scenes.say: Under pressure, each hybrid state gets one priority. Lowest goes first.

scenes.label: of KV memory: what one GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint costs
scenes.say: Why not checkpoint everywhere? On GLM five point three Flash, one checkpoint costs as much cache as twenty thousand tokens.

scenes.say: In the authors' replay of forty-eight coding agents, that's the gap between a thrashing cache and a healthy one.

scenes.text: A checkpoint earns its memory only where a turn resumes. In an agent loop, that is where the last turn ended.
